title: Longhorn
description: Cluster block storage: volume health, every volume ranked fullest first, the selected volumes' size, throughput, IOPS and latency, replica rebuilds, and each node's disk. Replaces the vendored Longhorn Example dashboard (grafana.com 13032). docs/design/longhorn.md.

panels.title: Volumes
panels.description: Longhorn volumes, attached or not.

panels.title: Healthy
panels.description: Volumes with every replica running and in sync.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: Volumes still serving with fewer than three healthy replicas, usually while one rebuilds. Longhorn exports one 0/1 series per state, so this selects state="degraded" == 1.

panels.title: Faulted
panels.description: Volumes with no healthy replica left: the data is unavailable until one is salvaged.

panels.title: Detached
panels.description: Volumes no node has attached, normally because their workload is scaled to zero. A detached volume's robustness is unknown, so it counts in neither Healthy nor Degraded.

panels.title: Rebuilding
panels.description: Replicas being rebuilt (engine mode WO): a node or replica came back, or a replica was rescheduled. Each copies the volume's data over 1 GbE.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Space on every Longhorn disk taken by anything, replicas or not, against the disks' total.

panels.title: Nodes not schedulable
panels.description: Longhorn nodes that are not ready, not schedulable, or have scheduling turned off. New replicas cannot land there.

panels.title: Volumes, fullest first
panels.description: One row per volume. Actual size is the space one replica takes on its disk, snapshots included, so Used can pass 100 % of capacity while snapshots hold overwritten blocks. In sync counts replicas the engine writes to (mode RW) out of three; detached volumes have no engine and read 0. Click a PVC to show only it below, or a namespace to open it.

targets.expr: max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) ((max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_robustness{state="unknown"}) == 1) * 0 + 0 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_robustness{state="healthy"}) == 1) * 0 + 1 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_robustness{state="degraded"}) == 1) * 0 + 2 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_robustness{state="faulted"}) == 1) * 0 + 3)

max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) ((max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="attached"}) == 1) * 0 + 1 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="detached"}) == 1) * 0 + 2 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="attaching"}) == 1) * 0 + 3 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="detaching"}) == 1) * 0 + 4 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="creating"}) == 1) * 0 + 5 or (max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_state{state="deleting"}) == 1) * 0 + 6)

count by (volume) (longhorn_engine_replica_mode{mode="RW"} == 1) * on (volume) group_left (pvc_namespace, pvc) (0 * max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_capacity_bytes) + 1) or 0 * max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_capacity_bytes)

count by (volume) (longhorn_engine_replica_mode{mode="WO"} == 1) * on (volume) group_left (pvc_namespace, pvc) (0 * max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_capacity_bytes) + 1) or 0 * max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_capacity_bytes)
max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_actual_size_bytes) / max by (pvc_namespace, pvc, volume) (longhorn_volume_capacity_bytes)

panels.title: Actual size
panels.description: Space one replica of each selected volume takes on disk, snapshots included.

panels.title: Used share
panels.description: Actual size over capacity. Above 100 % means snapshots hold blocks the filesystem has since overwritten.

panels.title: Read throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second the engine served to the workload. Reads come from the local replica where dataLocality placed one.

panels.title: Write throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second the workload wrote; every byte goes synchronously to all three replicas.

panels.title: Read IOPS
panels.description: Read operations per second.

panels.title: Write IOPS
panels.description: Write operations per second.

panels.title: Read latency (approximate)
panels.description: Mean read latency per volume. Approximate: Longhorn exports the mean latency of the operations in its last sampling window at scrape time (ns, shown here in seconds), not a quantile, so a spike between scrapes is missed and an idle volume reads 0.

panels.title: Write latency (approximate)
panels.description: Mean write latency per volume. Writes wait for the slowest replica, usually a Pi's USB disk over 1 GbE. Approximate: Longhorn exports the mean latency of the operations in its last sampling window at scrape time (ns, shown here in seconds), not a quantile, so a spike between scrapes is missed and an idle volume reads 0.

panels.title: Rebuilding and failed replicas
panels.description: Replicas the engine is rebuilding (mode WO) or has dropped (mode ERR), across every volume. Zero is the steady state.

panels.title: Volumes not healthy
panels.description: Volumes by robustness other than healthy. Degraded volumes still serve; faulted ones do not.

panels.title: Replicas by node
panels.description: Replicas each Longhorn node holds. Three replicas per volume with hard zone anti-affinity, where a zone is a physical host: the two VMs on one NUC share a zone.

panels.title: Physical hosts
panels.description: Longhorn's zone is the physical host: a VM's NUC (from Proxmox) or the Pi itself. Hard zone anti-affinity allows one replica of a volume per host, so Replicas and Volumes match; Extra copies above 0 means a host holds two replicas of one volume. Click a host to open it.

panels.title: Nodes, fullest first
panels.description: One row per Longhorn node: each worker contributes its /var/lib/longhorn on EPHEMERAL as one disk. Scheduled is the space promised to replicas placed there (their full capacity), which can pass Used by far. Reserved is Longhorn's 30 % hold-back. Click a node to open it.

panels.title: Disk used by node
panels.description: Space taken on each node's Longhorn disk, against the disk.

panels.title: Scheduled by node
panels.description: Space promised to the replicas on each node, against its disk. Longhorn refuses a new replica once this would pass the over-provisioning limit on the unreserved space.
